newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian shares soar on budget expectation.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian shares soar on budget expectation.

text.p: Nigerian shares rose to new heights on Friday as expectation heightened that the much-awaited 1997 budget could be released this weekend.
The all-share index closed at 7096.39 from 7085.78 on Thursday.
"Interest in stocks is strong in anticipation of the budget because the market expects an announcement on privatisation of state enterprises," one dealer said.
Besides gains among leading food and petroleum marketing shares, positive movements were recorded in the banking, agricultural and industrial sectors, dealers said.

Banks ended strongly, with Afribank witnessing an upturn, rising 10 kobo to 3.62 naira while FSB International Bank rose 25 kobo to 6.00 naira. United Bank for Africa was five kobo stronger at 6.75 naira.
Okomu Oilpalm was 9.10 naira, 10 kobo better.

Speculative trading pushed up prices of blue chips and oil marketers, with West African Portland Cement Company 30 kobo up at 48.70 naira while Industrial Gases, which turned in good full-year result, rose by the same margin to 12.30 naira.
Nestle rose to 51.65 naira, 30 kobo more, and the Coca-Cola bottlers Nigerian Bottling Company was at 31.55 naira, up 24 kobo.
But shares of Nigerian Breweries dipped in a renewed bout of sell-offs for the troubled stock.
One dealer said uncertainties in the sector were responsible for the shares closing 60 kobo down at 17.40 naira.
Minor losses were recorded by textile group Afprint and packaging firm Carnaud Metal Box (CMB).

Afprint shed one kobo to 2.59 naira on anxiety about the destruction by fire of a warehouse belonging to its subsidiary last week while CMB fell by the same amount to 2.80 naira because of the economic downturn in the sector. ($1=80 naira)
